site.name: Aaron Doubert
site.lead: Mechanical engineering at Purdue, graduating December 2027.
site.lead_sub: Control surfaces and mechanism design for Purdue Aerial Robotics, analog flight control electronics, and competition robots.

projects.title: PART ailerons and flaps
projects.summary: Hinge-moment sizing and printed construction for a 95 m/s airframe.

body.p: Hinge moments from a linearized thin-airfoil flap model (Roskam Part VI) at FAR 23 load factors — n = 10/3 rolling, n = 2 flaps down. Ruddervator modelled as a flat plate at its total angle to the flow, including an 8 m/s gust.
Printed shells with internal triangular ribs, turning on a bronze sleeve bushing at the hinge line. Control horn bolts on with M2 screws into heat-set inserts.

projects.title: Analog flight controller
projects.summary: Quadcopter PID loops computed in op-amps, not firmware.

body.p: Angle-to-rate loops on roll and pitch, rate-only on yaw, fed by an MPU-6050 through an ATtiny1614 and MCP4822 DACs. Board history: v1 → rev A → rev B, plus an SMT variant.

body.note: Rev 3 is failing on the bench. Write up what failed and what the next rev changes, and this note goes away.

shots.cap: Rev B — 90 × 210 mm, 4-layer, mounts on the frame.
Board on the 5-inch frame; dashed circles are the prop disks. Every trimpot stays reachable.

projects.title: Ping pong launcher
projects.summary: Ball flight with drag, Magnus lift and spin decay, and a solver that picks the shot.

body.p: Flight integrated with drag, Magnus lift and spin decay. A solver works backward from a target cup to a launch speed and spin; the launcher side sizes the flywheels for a three-wheel head.

body.note: No figures yet. Export main.m sections 2–3, the sweep plot and the animation GIF into img/, then add them to "shots" in projects.json.

projects.title: PART payload winch
projects.summary: Single-servo winch that lowers a payload under a 5 g limit and releases itself.

body.p: Replaced a rack-and-pinion gate concept with a 270° servo winch and a self-freeing TPU belt that unhooks from the spool pins. Became the team design. The three-pin belt is statically indeterminate; the 295 mm belt prints curved to fit the bed.

shots.cap: Final version on its rail mount.
One servo, spool and TPU retention belt.
Rail clip and slider, printed as separate parts for strength.
The sliding-wall deployer (v4) that came before the winch.
Demo test stand.

projects.title: Metal detector and audio equalizer
projects.summary: A two-555 beat-frequency metal detector and a 3-band audio EQ.

body.p: The detector oscillated at 71 kHz against a 50 kHz target and the square-wave mixing didn't beat cleanly, so the concept was proved in LTspice instead. The 3-band equalizer is the cleaner piece of the two.

projects.title: ASME battlebot and turret
projects.summary: An all-plastic spinner bot, a printed ball turret, and running the club as design lead.

body.p: Horizontal spinner with no metal armour: outrunner through a GT2 belt to a 6 × 1.5 in polycarbonate blade on a 36 mm flange, UHMWPE internals, PETG chassis. Led a four-person team. Now Design Lead — rules, CAD workshops and advising other teams.

projects.title: Dacora Motors
projects.summary: A rear console with a coffee maker that rises out of it, for a luxury EV prototype.

body.p: A DC motor drives a belt lift on linear rails; limit switches and a current-sensing stop handle the travel. Printed and CNC parts. Also made interface parts adapting the brake pedal and steering column to the vehicle.
